n3938cec7e88.s: As per the Economic Survey, without adequate health, education, skills and jobs for the working-age population, the demographic dividend may turn into a:
n3938cec7e88.x: The Economic Survey warns that failing to create these conditions could turn the dividend into a 'demographic nightmare'.

n92ebd57b321.s: Which of the following pairs (States – demographic phase) is correctly matched?
o: Bihar and Uttar Pradesh – Ageing phase
Kerala and Tamil Nadu – Ageing phase
Kerala and Tamil Nadu – Wide demographic window
n92ebd57b321.x: Kerala and Tamil Nadu are ageing States whose working-age share is already falling, which raises pension-related spending pressure. Bihar and UP have a wide window; Telangana and Uttarakhand a narrowing one.

n6634f1fa5f3.s: In which year did India's family planning programme adopt the target-free approach?
n6634f1fa5f3.x: The target-free approach came in 1996; 1976 was the year of the first National Population Policy.

nbb012c7d7b2.s: The National Population Policy, 2000 envisaged delivery of its services through:
nbb012c7d7b2.x: NPP 2000 followed a target-free, voluntary and informed-choice approach, with delivery through government, industry and NGOs.

n90b36e23b99.s: As per Census data, what is the major reason for the migration of women in India?
n90b36e23b99.x: Marriage is the major reason for women's migration, while work is the major reason for men's migration.

ndd97aa487e6.s: Which of the following pairs (migration theory – proponent) is NOT correctly matched?
o: Push-pull theory with intervening obstacles – Everett Lee
ndd97aa487e6.x: The Laws of Migration were given by E.G. Ravenstein, not Todaro; Todaro gave the expected-income rural-urban model and Lee the push-pull theory with intervening obstacles.

n278bc4761c6.s: Which of the following pairs (poverty measure – what it captures) is correctly matched?
n278bc4761c6.x: The Squared Poverty Gap gives more weight to the poorest and so measures severity; HCR measures incidence and PGI depth.

nc0a977b5c3b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Modified Mixed Reference Period (MMRP)?
o: It uses a 7-day recall period for some food items
It was first used for poverty estimation by the Tendulkar Committee
It records higher consumption than earlier recall periods
It gives a lower poverty estimate
nc0a977b5c3b.x: MMRP was first used by the Rangarajan group; Tendulkar moved from URP to MRP. MMRP's 7-day recall records 10-12% higher consumption and so lower poverty.

new.s: Who held that population grows geometrically while food supply grows only arithmetically?
new.x: T.R. Malthus (Principle of Population, 1798) contrasted geometric population growth with arithmetic growth of food.

new.s: The theory of optimum population, the population giving the highest income per head, is associated with:
new.x: Edwin Cannan propounded the optimum population theory: the population size that gives the highest income per head.

new.s: 'The Population Bomb' (1968), a Neo-Malthusian warning, was written by:
new.x: Paul Ehrlich wrote The Population Bomb (1968). Cannan is linked to optimum population and Notestein to demographic transition.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Frank Notestein gave the standard form of demographic transition theory in 1945. Optimum population is Cannan's, The Population Bomb Ehrlich's and the Principle of Population Malthus's.

new.s: In Malthusian theory, late marriage and moral restraint, which lower births, are called:
new.x: Malthus called measures that lower births (late marriage, restraint) preventive checks; positive checks raise deaths.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the demographic transition model?
o: Stage I – high birth rate, high death rate
Stage II – low birth rate, falling death rate
Stage III – falling birth rate, low death rate
Stage IV – low birth rate, low death rate
new.x: Stage II has a HIGH birth rate with a falling death rate, which produces a population explosion.

new.s: The Crude Birth Rate is the number of live births per 1,000 of the:
new.x: CBR and CDR are births and deaths per 1,000 mid-year population.

new.s: As per SRS 2024, which State has the highest Crude Birth Rate?
new.x: Bihar has the highest CBR (26.8) as per SRS 2024; Goa has the lowest (10.7).

new.s: As per SRS 2024, the lowest Crude Death Rate is recorded in:
new.x: Delhi has the lowest CDR (4.5), not Kerala; Chhattisgarh has the highest (8.4).

new.s: As per SRS 2024, which State has the lowest Crude Birth Rate?
new.x: Goa has the lowest CBR (10.7) as per SRS 2024, against India's 18.3.

new.s: India's Maternal Mortality Ratio in 2023 stood at:
new.x: India's MMR fell to 80.5 in 2023 from 130 in 2014-16.

new.s: The replacement level of Total Fertility Rate is:
new.x: A TFR of 2.1 is the replacement level at which a population replaces itself.

new.s: As per NFHS-5 (2019-21), India's Total Fertility Rate is:
new.x: India's TFR fell to 2.0 in NFHS-5 (from 2.2 in NFHS-4), below the replacement level of 2.1.

new.s: As per NFHS-5, which State has the highest Total Fertility Rate?
new.x: Bihar has the highest TFR (3.0) in NFHS-5; Meghalaya, UP and Jharkhand are also above 2.1 but lower.

new.s: As per NFHS-5, the Total Fertility Rate of Andhra Pradesh is:
new.x: Andhra Pradesh's TFR in NFHS-5 is 1.7, well below the replacement level of 2.1.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's fertility:
1. As per SRS 2024, India's TFR has been below replacement level for the fifth year running.
2. As per NFHS-5, India's TFR is above the replacement level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NFHS-5 TFR is 2.0, below the replacement level of 2.1.

new.s: India's demographic window of opportunity is placed at:
new.x: India's demographic window runs from 2005-06 to 2055-56.

new.s: According to the Economic Survey 2018-19, India's demographic dividend will peak around:
new.x: The dividend peaks around 2041, when the 20-59 age share reaches about 59%.

new.s: India's dependency ratio, 79% in 1975, had fallen to about what level by 2021?
new.x: The dependency ratio fell from 79% (1975) to 58% (2008) and about 48% (2021), mainly due to falling fertility.

new.s: India's female Labour Force Participation Rate in 2023-24 was:
new.x: Female LFPR rose from 23.3% in 2017-18 to 41.7% in 2023-24.

new.s: In the RBI typology of States, Telangana and Uttarakhand are placed in which demographic phase?
new.x: Telangana and Uttarakhand are in the narrowing (intermediate) phase; Kerala and TN are ageing; Bihar and UP have a wide, youthful window.

new.s: The median age of Andhra Pradesh's population is about:
new.x: AP's median age is 32.5, against India's 28.

new.s: After the Emergency sterilisations, India's family planning programme was renamed in 1977 as the:
new.x: In 1977 the programme was renamed the Family Welfare Programme after the forced sterilisations of the Emergency.

new.s: The Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) approach in India began in:
new.x: RCH began in 1997, a year after the 1996 target-free approach.

new.s: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment (1976) placed population control in the:
new.x: The 42nd Amendment put population control in the Concurrent List in 1976.

new.s: The immediate objective of the National Population Policy, 2000 was to:
o: meet the unmet need for contraception
new.x: The immediate objective was meeting the unmet need for contraception, with health infrastructure and integrated RCH services. TFR 2.1 was medium-term and stable population long-term.

new.s: The medium-term objective of NPP 2000 was to bring the TFR to replacement level by:
new.x: NPP 2000 aimed at TFR 2.1 by 2010 (medium-term); 2025 is the Mission Parivar Vikas target and 2045 the long-term stabilisation year.

new.s: Besides the Prime Minister as chairman, the National Commission on Population (2000) includes:
o: Members of the Rajya Sabha only
new.x: The Commission is chaired by the Prime Minister, and its members include Chief Ministers and Union ministers.

new.s: The State of World Population Report 2021, the first UN report on bodily autonomy, was titled:
o: Family Planning: Empowering People, Developing Nations
Empowering young people to create the families they want
new.x: UNFPA's SWOP 2021 (14 April 2021) was titled 'My Body is My Own'. The other options are World Population Day themes.

new.s: As per NFHS-6 (2023-24), India's Total Fertility Rate stood at:
new.x: NFHS-6, released on 29 May 2026, shows TFR steady at 2.0, with a contraceptive prevalence rate of 69.1%.

new.s: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana was earlier known as:
new.x: PMMVY was earlier called the Indira Gandhi Matritva Sahyog Yojana. JSY replaced the National Maternity Benefit Scheme.

new.s: Mission Parivar Vikas runs outreach teams in how many districts?
new.x: Mission Parivar Vikas covers 146 districts in 7 high-fertility States.

new.s: Mission Parivar Vikas aimed to bring the TFR down to 2.1 by:
new.x: Mission Parivar Vikas targets TFR 2.1 by 2025; NPP 2000 had targeted TFR 2.1 by 2010.

new.s: Under PMMVY, conditional cash aid is given through DBT for the:
new.x: PMMVY gives maternity benefit to pregnant and lactating women as conditional aid via DBT for the first live birth.

new.s: As per NFHS-5, the share of female sterilisation in India was:
new.x: Female sterilisation stood at 37.9% in NFHS-5; 69.1% is the NFHS-6 contraceptive prevalence rate.

new.s: Which State's Small Family Norms rules bar parents of more than two children from direct government recruitment from 1 January 2021?
new.x: Assam's Small Family Norms rules (2019) apply from 1 January 2021. UP only drafted a bill in July 2021.

new.s: The Uttar Pradesh draft Population (Control, Stabilisation and Welfare) Bill was released in:
new.x: UP released the draft Bill in July 2021; it was never passed.

new.s: As per Census 2011, about how many persons migrated during 2001-2011?
new.x: About 141.2 million persons moved during 2001-2011.

new.s: The largest migration stream in India, mostly of women and driven by marriage, is:
new.x: Rural to rural is the largest stream, mostly women moving for marriage; rural to urban is NOT the largest.

new.s: As per SRS 2024, the share of the elderly (60+) in India's population is:
new.x: The elderly are 9.7% of India's population (SRS 2024); Kerala has the highest share at 15%.

new.s: The National Policy on Older Persons, 1999 was framed by the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
new.x: The National Policy on Older Persons (1999) of the Ministry of Social Justice has 14 areas of intervention.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's draft population policy (March 2026) offers what incentive for a second or third child?
new.x: The draft policy offers ₹25,000 for a second or third child and removes the two-child norm for local body elections.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's draft Population Management Policy (March 2026):
1. It removes the two-child norm for local body elections.
2. It shifts the focus from population management to population control.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is reversed: the policy shifts from population control to population management.

new.s: Poverty judged by a person's own perception of their position is called:
new.x: Subjective poverty rests on a person's own perception of their position.

new.s: The capability approach to poverty is associated with:
new.x: Amartya Sen gave the capability approach; Oscar Lewis gave the culture of poverty.

new.s: Poverty caused temporarily by shocks, seasons or cycles is called:
new.x: Transient or cyclical poverty is temporary; chronic poverty lasts over long periods or across generations.

new.s: The calorie norm for the rural poverty line in India is, per capita per day:
new.x: The norm is 2,400 kcal per capita per day in rural areas and 2,100 kcal in urban areas.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a social indicator of poverty?
new.x: Illiteracy, lack of safe drinking water, poor housing and lack of jobs are social indicators; MPCE is the consumption basis of the poverty line itself.

new.s: The Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) covers which dimensions?
new.x: The MPI measures deprivation in health, education and living standards.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about poverty in India:
1. Lack of safe drinking water is a social indicator of poverty.
2. The official poverty line is fixed on the basis of literacy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the poverty line uses consumption, and literacy is not used to fix it.

new.s: As per the Rangarajan Expert Group, all-India poverty in 2011-12 was:
new.x: Rangarajan put poverty at 29.5% in 2011-12, against 21.9% by the Tendulkar method.

new.s: The Tendulkar poverty line has been criticised mainly as being:
new.x: Critics say the Tendulkar line is too low; it is based on consumption, not income or literacy.

new.s: Which survey of 2022-23 gave the first full MPCE update in over a decade?
new.x: MoSPI's HCES 2022-23 was the first full update of MPCE data in over a decade.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's poverty Head Count Ratio in 2011-12 was:
new.x: AP's HCR was 9.20% in 2011-12, against India's 21.92%.

new.s: The World Bank's $2.15-a-day international poverty line (2022) was based on which PPP base year?
new.x: The $2.15 line (2022) used 2017 PPP; $1.90 used 2011 PPP and the latest $3.00 uses 2021 PPP.

new.s: The World Bank's $1.25-a-day poverty line, set in 2008, used which PPP base year?
new.x: The $1.25 line (2008) was based on 2005 PPP; the $1 line (1990) on 1985 PPP.

new.s: According to the World Bank (2018), which country may already have overtaken India as the country with the most extreme poor?
new.x: The World Bank noted in 2018 that Nigeria may have overtaken India in the number of extreme poor.

new.s: Under the old $1.25 line, India's number of poor rose from 421 million in 1981 to about:
new.x: Under the $1.25 line, India's poor rose from 421 million (1981) to 456 million (2005).

new.s: The First UN Decade for the Eradication of Poverty covered the period:
new.x: The First UN Decade (res. 50/107) ran from 1997 to 2006; the second from 2008 to 2017 and the third from 2018 to 2027.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Second UN Decade for the Eradication of Poverty – 1997-2006
Third UN Decade for the Eradication of Poverty – 2018-2027
new.x: The Third UN Decade runs 2018-2027. The Second Decade was 2008-2017, SDG 1 targets 2030 and absolute poverty was defined in 1995 at Copenhagen.

new.s: The theme of the Second UN Decade for the Eradication of Poverty (2008-2017) was:
o: End poverty in all its forms everywhere
Full employment and decent work for all
new.x: The Second Decade's theme was 'Full employment and decent work for all'; 'End poverty in all its forms everywhere' is SDG 1.
